subject.title: [security] Git seed sends credential-bearing remote URLs to lease runners

question: Should Crabbox fail closed or skip git seed when the local Git remote URL contains userinfo?
rationale: Both choices protect the credential boundary, but they have different operator impact: fail-closed makes the unsafe remote explicit, while skip-and-overlay preserves run progress with less visibility.

options.title: Fail closed with redacted diagnostic
options.body: Return a clear error before any lease-runner command is constructed and identify only that the remote contains URL userinfo.

options.title: Skip git seed and continue overlay sync
options.body: Disable git seed for that run and rely on rsync/archive overlay, emitting a redacted warning so credentials are not sent to the lease.

options.title: Design explicit private seed credentials
options.body: Keep private-repo seeding only behind a separate scoped delivery mechanism that avoids argv and persisted remote config.

recommendation.title: Fail closed with redacted diagnostic
recommendation.body: Return a clear error before any lease-runner command is constructed and identify only that the remote contains URL userinfo.

likelyOwner.reason: The central git-seed and security-boundary paths are most strongly tied to this owner in current-main history.
